newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: INTERVIEW-Bank of Ireland says outlook good.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Bank of Ireland says outlook good.

text.p: Bank of Ireland said the outlook for the year ahead was very positive although lending growth had slowed slightly in the second half.
"It may not be as strong as it was in this 12-month period but I think it will continue. I think it will be good," chief executive Pat Molloy told Reuters in an interview.
He noted there was some concern about inflationary pressures in the Irish economy but said he saw no reason to worry.

"From my own point of view, I wouldn't say there is any serious cause for concern. I think the economy is being managed very well and I think the outlook for the year ahead is very positive," he said.
Molloy said Bank of Ireland was currently going through a period of change which should leave it well placed to achieve further growth.
The bank, one of Ireland's largest banking and financial services groups, reported half-year pre-tax profits of 193.1 million punts compared with 191.8 million a year earlier.
The results were in line with analysts' expectations which ranged from 190 to 194 million punts.
"The results were bang in line with expectations and those expectations were conditioned by the fact that this is very much a transition year," Molloy said.
In April, Bank of Ireland merged its U.S. operation, First Holdings, with Royal Bank of Scotland's Citzens Financial Group in which it now has a 23.5 percent interest.
This involved a number of once-off restructuring costs and also has a significant after-tax effect as Bank of Ireland's earnings from the U.S. are now taxable.

It also announced it was acquiring Bristol & West, Britain's ninth largest building society, for 600 million stg in April while a number of restructuring and re-engineering projects are underway in its retail division, involving extra staff.
"It's a transition year in those respects but at the end of it all I think we are going to be very strongly positioned for continuing growth."
Molloy said the group was paying for Bristol & West in cash which meant it would not have a lot of spending power left after the acquisition was completed in mid-1997.
"We will begin to build capital thereafter relatively quickly. That is going to be the dominant issue for us in the course of the next calendar year."
He said the bank was putting a lot of effort and investment into areas such as expanding its asset management business and its new direct banking operation.
In the U.S., Citizens recently acquired two banks and is continuing a relatively aggressive acquisitions programme, Molloy said. "We are very anxious to see it continuing on that trend," he added.
The bank's share price was unchanged at 511 by 0933 GMT.
